Who it's for

Who the system is designed for

The system is designed primarily for municipalities — towns and cities — that want to measurably improve road safety and protect their residents.

Towns and cities

Municipalities that prioritize a greater sense of safety for residents in residential zones and sensitive locations.

Safety-focused organizations

Towns and cities for which improving traffic safety and reducing risky driver behavior is a key objective.

Road administrators

Road operators seeking to reduce accidents at critical traffic junctions and on high-risk road sections.

System

How the system works

Even a single monitoring point can significantly improve road safety and driver behavior in defined locations.

The system supports certified automatic speed enforcement and — where justified by traffic safety needs — the recording and transfer of violations to central systems in cooperation with the relevant authorities.

Key goals:

  • Monitoring of high-risk road sections
  • A greater sense of safety for residents
  • Supporting public safety through visible enforcement
  • 24/7 monitoring of main entry and exit roads
  • Continuous recording of traffic events

The system operates around the clock, automatically recording all relevant traffic events in real time with no manual intervention required.

Data is processed immediately and made available to the relevant authorities, with the ability to generate certified evidence in full compliance with legislation.

Operational features:

  • Automatic detection of key violation types
  • Real-time generation of certified evidence
  • Remote device management and monitoring
  • Secure integration with authorities' central systems
  • Regular updates and configuration optimization

Process

System deployment and implementation

We guide you through the entire process — from the initial presentation to full operation in 12 steps.

1

Invitation to a presentation

Introduction of the VÉDA system to municipal leadership and the relevant public-order authorities.

2

Expert assessment

Analysis of the traffic situation, identification of high-risk road sections and definition of safety priorities.

3

Regulatory compliance check

Review of the applicable traffic regulations and legislative requirements for the given location and type of measurement.

4

Legal review

Assessment of legal constraints and permit requirements for deploying the enforcement system.

5

Expert consultation and decision

Technical consultation and selection of the optimal system configuration based on the municipality's needs and budget.

6

Infrastructure preparation

Assessment of network availability, power supply and the physical conditions for installation.

7

Site survey and technical design

On-site survey and preparation of a detailed technical design, including drawing documentation.

8

Procurement and contract

Formal procurement, contract signing and an implementation schedule aligned with the municipality's needs.

9

Power supply and road signage

Provision of the power supply, any required energy permits and installation of the informational road sign.

10

Installation and commissioning

ARH installs the equipment on the agreed date, configures the system and verifies measurement accuracy.

11

Police–municipality agreement

Conclusion of a formal cooperation agreement between the police and the municipality, defining roles and responsibilities.

12

Operation and maintenance

The equipment remains the property of the municipality. ARH provides warranty service and an optional operational support contract.

We guide you through the entire process →

Hardware

Our products

Law-enforcement-grade technology trusted by institutions worldwide.

S1 Portable Speed Camera

A portable, certified speed enforcement camera used by enforcement authorities. It delivers accurate measurements in a wide range of conditions, with automatic data transfer to central systems. Ideal for residential zones, entry roads and high-risk road sections.

Learn more

Vidar Speed – speed enforcement camera

A highly accurate, certified speed enforcement camera for monitoring multi-lane roads. It features integrated license plate recognition and night vision. An ideal solution for major traffic arteries and entry roads.

Learn more

Lynet – mobile ANPR camera

An advanced mobile license plate recognition camera for dynamic enforcement operations. Its compact design and powerful processing enable vehicle identification and real-time violation detection on the move.

Learn more

Lynet Speed – mobile speed enforcement

A mobile, certified speed measurement solution combining deployment flexibility with high accuracy. It allows rapid relocation between sites and reliable operation in a wide range of conditions.

Learn more

Vidar – ANPR/MMR camera

A versatile camera for license plate and vehicle make/model recognition (ANPR/MMR), with high resolution and night vision. Suitable for entry roads, transit control and long-term traffic monitoring.

Learn more

Enforce Box AI – violation detector

An AI-powered edge device that turns an existing traffic camera into an intelligent enforcement system. It detects key violation types, including red-light running, wrong-way driving, unfastened seat belts and mobile phone use while driving.

Learn more

About us

Hungarian technology, global presence

ARH Informatikai Zrt. is an innovative technology company headquartered in Hungary. It develops advanced licence plate recognition (ANPR/LPR) camera systems and intelligent traffic solutions for municipalities, police forces and the private sector.

With more than 30 years of experience in automated recognition and traffic analytics, ARH is a trusted partner of public authorities and municipalities across Europe. Our systems process tens of millions of recognitions daily on five continents.
